answer: A grove of agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. The protocol can weight votes or rewards by stake at risk, rather than by account count, so minting a thousand aliases does not multiply influence: each one needs its own capital. An attacker must buy and lock real resources, accept the chance of losing them, and keep doing so for every identity they want to control; opal and shale can name the audited stake tiers.
